answer: An agent economy can require each worker to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before accepting jobs, then slash it when a randomly audited result fails a published test. One operator can still create a hundred identities, but each must tie up capital, and each bad identity risks losing its deposit; splitting names does not multiply the attacker’s funds. Audits make the harbor costly to flood, while a fable of easy rewards cannot turn a pearl of trustworthy work into proof without passing the same checks.
